evidence.source_sentence: The lack of toughness and heat resistance of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) limit its application in construction, transportation, packaging, and medical treatment.
In this work, the core–shell structure polybutadiene grafted styrene and acrylonitrile copolymer (PB-g-SAN), named (ABS), was utilized to toughen PVC.
The heat-resistant modifier styrene-N-phenylmaleimide-acrylonitrile terpolymer (SMIA) synthesized by bulk polymerization was added to PVC/ABS to improve the heat resistance of the composite.

The Vicat softening temperature of the ternary functional composite (PVC/ABS/SMIA, 72:8:20) raised by $2 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$, and the initial decomposition temperature increased by $1 9 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$.

Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) resin has attracted wide attention in construction, transportation, packaging, and medical applications because of its low cost, corrosion resistance, and flame retardancy [1–3].

The polybutadiene grafted styrene and acrylonitrile copolymer (PB-g-SAN), named (ABS), is a class of core–shell graft copolymer modifiers synthesized by emulsion polymerization, with polybutadiene (PBL) rubber as the core and polystyrene-co-acrylonitrile as the shell [12].

Blending with components possessing high glass transition temperature is a selectable method to elevate the heat resistance of PVC [17].

Fewer studies have been reported on the modification of PVC resins using the styrene-N-phenylmaleimide-acrylonitrile terpolymer.
In this work, the heat-resistant modifier styrene-N-phenylmaleimideacrylonitrile copolymer (SMIA) was synthesized.

3.2 | The Brittle-Tough Transition and Characterization of PVC/ABS Composites

The brittle-toughness fracture transition point of PVC resin toughened with ABS is crucial to the performance of composites, which was searched by adjusting the content of ABS core– shell toughened particles.
